text:
maya: thinking out loud — propose a tiny "roaming index" approach for weight streaming. goal: enable lazy reads of quantized chunks without a big manifest and with simple integrity checks.

sam: curious, what does roaming index buy vs current per-shard manifest?

maya: two things: 1) tiny index for offsets+checksums that can be embedded at end of shard (append-only) so we can mmap most shards but still locate quant chunks; 2) allow a lightweight header-free fetch in object stores (pull tail, parse index, then range get needed chunks). avoids a separate manifest service.

ravi: how do we handle versioning? if we change quant layout we need a compat marker.

maya: include a 1-line schema tag + monotonic format version in the index. e.g. `v:1;fmt:roam-q;flags:has-checksums` — on mismatch fallback to full manifest path.

jen: can we see a sample index layout?

maya: yep, example tail blob (binary friendly but shown as pseudo-json):
```
{"schema":"roam-q","version":1,"shard_id":"s0","chunks":[{"id":0,"off":1024,"len":131072,"crc":3452345},{"id":1,"off":132096,"len":131072,"crc":8932452}],"footer_crc":999128}
```

sam: i like tail-anchored index. cheaper for small models and no separate manifest. but what about partial shard uploads and multipart uploads? index might not land atomically.

maya: plan: uploader writes shard body, uploads index as last part; storage-level atomicity (S3 multipart finalize) guarantees tail is present only after complete upload. for local/oss we keep a short-sideband marker file during staging, then rename.

ravi: runtime handling: if index missing, we fall back to existing manifest lookup+full shard read? that's expensive for cold paths.

maya: fallback: try naive tail read -> if not present, attempt a small-range probe for a footer magic string. if still not found, route to manifest service. also opportunistic background index generation server-side for hot shards.

jen: ops question — how do we avoid many small ranged reads becoming the new cost?

maya: two mitigations: 1) cache index in local shard cache keyed by shard etag, 2) batch range requests for contiguous chunks and use a per-request aggregator that merges ranges. plus heuristics: if model is small (<100MB) prefer full GET and cache.

sam: integrity checks? CRC in index is good. do we need per-chunk hash (sha1) for extra safety?

maya: crc32 for perf, but we expose a strict mode controlled by config where we verify sha256 for regulated customers. default: crc is fine and fast.

ravi: sounds reasonable. can we prototype with a single-quant format first (4-bit Q4) and measure latency & extra GETs per cold-start?

maya: yep. my plan: PoC branch that writes roaming index in our weight-writer, a shim loader that prefers roaming index, and a small harness that simulates cold RPCs to object store. target numbers: <2 extra range requests per shard on average, <5% cold-start latency overhead.

jen: add a flag to Redwood runtime to disable roaming-index per deployment for troubleshooting.

maya: will do. also adding metrics: index-hit, index-miss, fallback-to-manifest, extra-range-requests, average-range-bytes.

ci-bot: CI: test matrix queued for branch `roam-index-poc` — unit tests + integration storage-sim.

sam: ok if maya posts short RFC blurb + experiment plan we can decide after numbers.

maya: will open short RFC and a PR with the PoC by EOD Wed. thanks all :rocket:
